options.extendedDescription: How many transcoding jobs can run at the same time. Each transcoder handles one job, so this is your parallelism limit. Extra jobs are not rejected, they queue and start as slots free up. It only scales up under a real backlog, and each running transcoder costs tokens, so this doubles as your cost ceiling. Default 2. Keep it at 1 while testing, raise it when you need batches done faster.

options.name: EncoreMinInstances
options.label: EncoreMinInstances
options.description: Configuration option for encoremininstances
options.extendedDescription: The number of transcoder instances kept running even when there is no work. Default is 0, which is almost always what you want: it lets the stack scale all the way down so you pay nothing for transcoding while idle. Setting it to 1 or more removes the wait before the first job starts, but you then pay the full daily rate per instance around the clock whether anything is transcoding or not.

options.name: EncoreIdleTimeoutMs
options.label: EncoreIdleTimeoutMs
options.description: Timeout value in milliseconds or seconds
options.extendedDescription: How long an idle transcoder waits before shutting itself down, in milliseconds. A shorter value saves tokens but means a job arriving shortly after the last one pays the startup delay again. A longer value keeps a warm instance ready at the cost of paying for that idle time. If you submit jobs in bursts, set this longer than the typical gap within a burst.

options.description: Username for SPX authentication. If provided along with password, users will be required to login to access the application.
options.extendedDescription: The README mentions that if username is present but password is blank, the app will ask for login policy on first launch. Username and password are stored in config.json, with password being encrypted.

options.name: Password
options.label: Password
options.description: Password for SPX authentication. Works in conjunction with username to enable login protection for the application.
options.extendedDescription: When both username and password are provided, password is stored encrypted in config.json. If username exists but password is blank, the application prompts for login policy configuration.

options.name: S3TemplatesUrl
options.label: S3TemplatesUrl
options.description: S3 bucket URL or path for storing and retrieving HTML graphics templates used by SPX for live production graphics.
options.extendedDescription: Templates are HTML files with SPXGCTemplateDefinition objects that define lower thirds, bumpers, logos and other on-screen graphics. Normally stored in ASSETS/templates folder but can be hosted on S3 for cloud deployments.

options.name: S3ProjectsUrl
options.label: S3ProjectsUrl
options.description: S3 bucket URL or path for storing SPX projects and rundowns data that would normally be stored in the DATAROOT folder.
options.extendedDescription: Projects contain rundowns (playlists) and settings. Each project has subfolders with rundown JSON files and profile.json for project-specific settings like assigned templates and custom controls.

options.name: S3PluginsUrl
options.label: S3PluginsUrl
options.description: Configures the S3 bucket URL for storing SPX plugins and extensions. Plugins provide additional functionality like custom controls and user interface panels.
options.extendedDescription: The README mentions that plugins are stored in the ASSETS/plugins folder and provide additional functionality such as custom function buttons and extensions with independent user interfaces.

options.name: S3MediaUrl
options.label: S3MediaUrl
options.description: Configures the S3 bucket URL for storing media assets like images, videos, and other files used by graphics templates.
options.extendedDescription: Media files are normally stored in the ASSETS/media folder structure with subfolders for images, videos, etc. Templates can reference these files using the filelist field type in template definitions.

options.name: S3JsonUrl
options.label: S3JsonUrl
options.description: Specifies the S3 bucket URL for storing and retrieving JSON data files used for data-driven graphics and external data integration.
options.extendedDescription: JSON data can be used for automated workflows and data-driven graphics, supporting SPX's capability for 100% automated workflows mentioned in the README.

options.name: S3EndpointUrl
options.label: S3EndpointUrl
options.description: Custom S3-compatible endpoint URL for accessing object storage services other than AWS S3, such as MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, or other S3-compatible storage providers.
options.extendedDescription: Used when connecting to non-AWS S3-compatible storage services. If not specified, defaults to standard AWS S3 endpoints.

options.name: S3AccessKeyId
options.label: S3AccessKeyId
options.description: AWS access key ID for authenticating with S3 services to access templates, projects, and media assets stored in cloud storage.
options.extendedDescription: Required credential for accessing AWS S3 or S3-compatible storage services. Used in conjunction with secret access key for authentication.

options.name: S3SecretAccessKey
options.label: S3SecretAccessKey
options.description: AWS secret access key for authenticating with S3 services, paired with the access key ID for secure cloud storage access.
options.extendedDescription: Secret credential used with access key ID for S3 authentication. Should be kept secure and not exposed in logs or client-side code.

options.name: S3Region
options.label: S3Region
options.description: AWS region identifier specifying the geographical region where the S3 buckets are located for optimal performance and compliance.
options.extendedDescription: Determines which AWS region to connect to for S3 services. Examples include 'us-east-1', 'eu-west-1', etc. Important for latency and data residency requirements.

options.name: InitFrontendApiTokens

options.extendedDescription: The README shows backend SDKs use Unleash API URL 'http://localhost:4242/api/' with API token 'default:development.unleash-insecure-api-token'. Unleash supports 15+ official backend SDKs including Go, Java, Node.js, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, and .NET.
